title: 'Lyrical Ballads,' and Other Poems, 1797-1800
reliability_notes: The standard scholarly text of Wordsworth's early and Lyrical Ballads poems with full textual history; Ithaca: Cornell University Press, confirmed by library catalogue records and by the series listing in Cambridge bibliographies. Earlier attributions of this edition to Penguin are incorrect.

title: William Wordsworth: The Major Works
reliability_notes: One-volume poems, The Prelude and selected prose in chronological text states; first published 1984 and revised in later reissues, so citations may give a later impression year for the same text.

title: The Prelude: 1799, 1805, 1850 (Norton Critical Edition)
author_or_editor: Jonathan Wordsworth, M. H. Abrams and Stephen J. Gill (editors)
reliability_notes: The first edition to print all three recensions of The Prelude together, with commentary and critical essays; the usual scholarly basis for dating the 1799, 1805 and 1850 texts.

title: The Complete Poetical Works of Samuel Taylor Coleridge (2 volumes)
reliability_notes: The older collected text of Coleridge's poetry, still the source of many standard readings; superseded in matters of chronology and variant text by the Bollingen Collected Works.

title: Biographia Literaria (The Collected Works of Samuel Taylor Coleridge, volume 7)
author_or_editor: James Engell and W. Jackson Bate (editors)
publisher: Routledge and Kegan Paul / Princeton University Press
reliability_notes: The critical edition of Coleridge's literary autobiography with full apparatus; the authoritative text for chapters 14, 17 and 22 and for the distinction of imagination from fancy.

title: The Collected Works of Samuel Taylor Coleridge (16 volumes)
publisher: Routledge and Kegan Paul / Princeton University Press
reliability_notes: The Bollingen series, the backbone citation for Coleridge's prose, notebooks and marginalia. A university finding aid dates the run 1971-2001; some bibliographies give 1969-2002, so volume years should be checked individually.

title: Lord Byron: The Major Works
reliability_notes: Standard one-volume Byron, poetry with selected letters and life writings. The year recorded is the current Oxford World's Classics issue evidenced on the publisher's page; the earlier hardback impression of the same edition is not separately confirmed here.

title: The Complete Poetical Works of Lord Byron (7 volumes)
reliability_notes: The modern critical Byron text, published 1980-1993; it supersedes the older Murray edition edited by E. H. Coleridge for scholarly reference to the poems.

title: Byron's Letters and Journals (12 volumes with index and supplement)
reliability_notes: The scholarly Byron correspondence, London, 1973-1994. Volume counts differ between accounts (eleven text volumes with index, or thirteen including the index and the 1994 supplement), so cite the individual volume year.

title: Shelley's Poetry and Prose (Norton Critical Edition)
author_or_editor: Donald H. Reiman and Sharon B. Powers (editors)
reliability_notes: The most widely used accurate one-volume Shelley, with textual notes and criticism; a later revised edition by Reiman and Fraistat carries the same authority under a different imprint year.

title: The Poems of John Keats
reliability_notes: The first fully authoritative text of Keats's poems, established from manuscript and first-edition collation; the standard basis for dating revisions and for the variant readings of the 1819 odes.

title: John Keats: The Complete Poems (Penguin Classics)
reliability_notes: The Penguin text of Keats, revised in 1988 and reissued subsequently (a 2006 impression is current in libraries). The year of the first Penguin impression is not confirmed by the records consulted, so the revised edition is cited.

title: The Letters of John Keats, 1814-1821 (2 volumes)
reliability_notes: The definitive scholarly edition of Keats's correspondence, with the manuscript readings and dating that later editions follow.

title: The Complete Poetry and Prose of William Blake
reliability_notes: The standard one-volume Blake with commentary; first published 1965 and reissued in a newly revised edition in 1988. No evidence was found for a further revision by another editor, so the 1988 text is cited.

title: The William Blake Archive
author_or_editor: Morris Eaves, Robert N. Essick and Joseph Viscomi (general editors)
reliability_notes: Facsimiles and transcriptions of Blake's illuminated and printed works with physical-catalogue data; founded 1993 and launched 1996, supported by the Library of Congress and the National Endowment for the Humanities. Essential for the dating of individual illuminated copies.

title: The Cambridge Edition of the Works of Jane Austen
reliability_notes: The collated scholarly text of the six completed novels and the minor and unfinished works, issued 2005-2008, with full textual notes on the early editions.

title: The Edinburgh Edition of the Waverley Novels
reliability_notes: The critical edition of Scott's fiction from manuscript and first-edition evidence, begun in 1993; individual volume years vary, so cite the volume rather than the series start.

title: The Edinburgh Edition of Walter Scott's 'Minstrelsy of the Scottish Border' (3 volumes)
author_or_editor: Sigrid Rieuwerts (editor, with Katherine Campbell and Emily Lyle)
reliability_notes: The modern scholarly text of Scott's border ballads with the suppressed and variant readings. The publisher listed the set in its August 2014 to January 2015 new-titles catalogue, so the volume year should be confirmed against the copy used.

title: Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus: The 1818 Text
reliability_notes: The edition that re-established the original 1818 text against the 1831 revision, with the textual note that dates the change; the basis for most current scholarship on Mary Shelley's first version.

title: The Cambridge Companion to British Romanticism
reliability_notes: Essays on the generation, its forms and its afterlives; a second edition appeared in 2010 with the same general editorship. Earlier attributions of the volume to a different editor are incorrect.

title: The Works of Thomas De Quincey (21 volumes)
reliability_notes: The complete scholarly De Quincey, London, 2000-2003, establishing texts and dating for the confessions, the opium writings and the essays.

title: Confessions of an English Opium-Eater and Other Writings (Oxford World's Classics)
reliability_notes: A reliable single-volume text of the confessions with introduction and notes, used where the twenty-one-volume edition is not at hand.

title: The Complete Works of William Hazlitt (21 volumes)
reliability_notes: The collected Hazlitt, London, 1930-1934, still the standard reference for the essays, criticism and table-talk, though its texts are older than current scholarly practice.

title: The Works of Charles and Mary Lamb (7 volumes)
reliability_notes: The standard collected Lamb, London, 1903-1905, in seven volumes including Charles's essays, the joint writings and the letters; other editors have been credited with this set in error. Earlier records here gave six volumes, which the publisher's run of the Lucas edition does not support.

title: The Norton Anthology of American Literature (9th edition)
reliability_notes: The standard classroom anthology of American writing; volume A to 1820 and the opening of volume B cover the early-republic strand of this installment, with reliable headnotes and textual notes.

title: Washington Irving: History, Tales, and Sketches (Library of America)
reliability_notes: Authoritative texts of the Sketch Book, the historical works and the tales, with textual notes on the revised editions Irving prepared.

title: Washington Irving: Three Western Narratives (Library of America)
reliability_notes: The frontier and Rocky Mountain narratives with introduction and notes, the standard modern text for Irving's western writing.

title: James Fenimore Cooper: The Leatherstocking Tales (2 volumes, Library of America)
reliability_notes: The five frontier novels in established texts with textual notes; the usual scholarly basis for quoting Cooper's wilderness fiction.

title: The Novels and Related Works of Charles Brockden Brown: Bicentennial Edition
author_or_editor: Sydney J. Krause (general editor); S. W. Reid (textual editor)
reliability_notes: The critical edition of Brown's novels from the first editions, begun in 1977; the total volume count of the Bicentennial set should be verified against the copy consulted.

title: The Collected Writings of Charles Brockden Brown
publisher: Bucknell University Press (distributed by Rowman and Littlefield)
reliability_notes: The successor scholarly series gathering Brown's non-novelistic writings (letters, political pamphlets, journalism), issued volume by volume from volume one, 'Letters and Early Epistolary Writings', in 2013. The series is still in progress, so no fixed total volume count is asserted; later volumes carry their own editors and years.

title: The Works of Maria Edgeworth (12 volumes)
reliability_notes: The collected Edgeworth, London, 1999-2003, with textual notes on the early editions; the set is titled The Works, not Collected Works, and the publisher is sometimes misstated.

title: An American Dictionary of the English Language (2 volumes)
reliability_notes: Webster's foundational American dictionary, printed in two quarto volumes; cited for the history of American letters and spelling reform rather than as a literary text.

title: The Letters of William Cullen Bryant (6 volumes)
author_or_editor: Thomas G. Voss (editor); William Cullen Bryant II
reliability_notes: The scholarly Bryant correspondence, New York, 1975-1992, the best evidence for the dating of his poems and his editorship of the Evening Post. A modern standard edition of Bryant's poetical works was not verified.

title: The North American Review
author_or_editor: Founded in Boston in 1815 by William Tudor and associates; edited from 1823 by Jared Sparks
reliability_notes: The principal American literary review of the early republic, the venue for Bryant, Channing and the debate on a national literature. The proprietors and imprints changed with the decades, so individual issues should be cited by volume and date.

title: The Papers of Thomas Jefferson
reliability_notes: The edition begun in 1943 as a partnership of Princeton University and its press; volume one appeared in 1950 and remains the standard scholarly text for Jefferson's writings and papers of the period.
